card.name: Timing of when to take a dose
card.fires_on: Words inside instructions about when to take a drug relative to an event, such as 'at least 2 hours before', 'approximately 1 hour before sexual activity' or 'at the same time each day'. It also fires on a drug name just before such timing.

modes.label: Before-event timing
modes.description: Words leading into or following 'X hours before' a meal, activity or other drug.
modes.example: approximately 30 minutes before<< sexual>> activity. The lowest dose that provides benefit

modes.label: Dose wording before timing
modes.description: A verb, drug name or comma in a dosing sentence that is about to give a time window.
modes.example: cefdinir for oral suspension should be<< taken>> at least 2 hours before or after

modes.label: Same time each day
modes.description: Words in instructions to dose at a consistent time.
modes.example: Administer IMBRUVICA at approximately the same<< time>> each day.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about lasting or time-limited effect, such as validity period and long-acting, and away from unrelated tokens.
card.plain: It lights up in dosing directions that say when to take a medicine, such as hours before an activity or another drug.
